To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we can achieve speedups of 2.2 for a multigrid solver on a cluster using GPUs.
the performance of a multigrid based FE solver can be improved by a factor of 2 or more by using GPUs for coarse grid computations.

we can achieve speedups of two to more for large problems on a cluster of GPUs by using a combination of coarse-grained and fine-grained GPU parallelism and a mixed precision iterative refinement technique.

the presented approach is very promising for the use of GPUs in FE simulations.
the GPU-based approach is a promising way to improve the performance of a multigrid-based FE simulation on clusters.

the use of GPUs in a cluster setting is a very viable approach to accelerate FE simulations, and that the use of a mixed precision, multigrid solver is a very promising technique to overcome the limited precision of current GPUs.

we have successfully integrated GPU-accelerated multigrid solv- ers into an existing software framework.

GPUs can be used to improve the performance of a parallel FE solver on a cluster, while at the same time reducing the overall energy consumption of the system.
the use of GPUs for the acceleration of FE simulations is feasible, and that the use of a mixed precision, multigrid solver is a promising approach to overcome precision limitations on GPUs.
